newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-GUATEMALA REMAIN ALIVE IN WORLD CUP HUNT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUATEMALA REMAIN ALIVE IN WORLD CUP HUNT.

text.p: Guatemala, forced to play home World Cup qualifying matches on the road because of a stampede that killed 84 fans in October, stayed alive in the hunt for a World Cup berth with a 2-1 win over Trinidad and Tobago on Sunday.
Julio Rodas was the hero, scoring two brilliant goals in front of a partisan crowd at the Coliseum in Los Angeles, which has the largest population of Guatemalans outside of Guatemala.
The win opened up the race in CONCACAF Group A between the United States, Costa Rica and Guatemala for a World Cup berth.
Two teams will go on to the semifinal round to decide the three teams from the North America, Central America and Caribbean region that will advance to the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
The United States and Costa Rica each have nine points in the four-nation group A and face each other in what could be a crucial match next Saturday in Palo Alto, California.
Guatemala, with seven points, has one remaining match against the United States in El Salvador in two weeks.

Guatemala dominated the first half Sunday and missed several chances before going ahead in the 27th minute when full-back Martin Machon overlapped on the left wing. Everaldo Valencia dummied over his low cross and the ball went to Rodas, who buried a low left-foot shot from six meters past goalkeeper Ross Russell.

The Trinidadians, who have already been elimated from World Cup contention and were playing without English Premier League star striker Dwight Yorke, equalised three minutes later when Angus Eve's shot from the edge of the box hit defender Eduardo Acevedo and rolled past keeper Edgar Estrada.
But Rodas put Guatemala ahead for good in the 60th minute when Juan Plata's vicious volley came back off the cross bar and Rodas dived to head in the rebound from 12 meters out.

Guatemala was officially designated the home team in Los Angeles following a FIFA order to play its home games away from the Mateo Flores satdium in Guatemala City following the tragedy there on October 16.
The Guatemalan players wore black armbands and there was a minute's silence before the kickoff in memory of the the fans who died.

Lineups: Guatemala - Edgar Estrada, Martin Machon, Eduardo Acevedo, Erik Miranda, Julio Giron, German Ruano, Julio Rodas (Juan Torres 81st minute), Jorge Rodas, Juan Plata (Carlos Lemus 77th),Manuel Funes, Everaldo Valencia (Mario Acevedo 50th)

Trinidad and Tobago - Ross Russell, Alvin Thomas, Dexter Francis, Ancil Elcock (Marvin Andrews 52nd), Marvin Faustin, Richard Theodore (Hutson Charles, 73rd), Anthony Rougier (Jerry St. Louis, 80th), David Nakhid, Angus Eve, Jerred Nixon, Stern John
